definition.overflow_avoidance: No n+d-1 expression is used. n*M is evaluated as an unsigned 64-bit product; for n<=2^32-1 and M<2^32 it is below 2^64. q0*d<=n<=2^32-1, b*d<=131071*43=5636053, and the corrected ceiling fits u32.

proof_sketch.ceil_identity: For the exact quotient case rem<=d-1 and q0+(rem!=0)+(rem>d) is ceil(n/d). For the one-low case rem=d+r: if r=0 the correction is 1; if r>0 it is 2. This computes ceil(n/d) without forming n+d-1.
proof_sketch.predicate_identity: For positive d and integer b>=0, n>b*d is equivalent to n/d>b, which is equivalent to ceil(n/d)>b because ceil preserves the strict integer threshold. Thus n>b*d iff b<ceil(n/d).
proof_sketch.quotient_bound: M=floor(2^32/d) gives M/2^32 <= 1/d, hence q0<=floor(n/d). Also M>2^32/d-1 and 0<=n<2^32 imply n*M/2^32>n/d-1, so q0>=floor(n/d)-1.
proof_sketch.remainder_bound: If q0=floor(n/d), rem is the ordinary remainder in [0,d-1]. If q0=floor(n/d)-1, rem is d plus that remainder in [d,2d-1].

scope: Unsigned integer model only; no RTL, simulation, synthesis, placement, routing, timing, CDC, hardware, or codec-performance claim.
verification_notes: All arithmetic comparisons use Python exact integers after constraining n to u32 and b to u17.
The three divisors are odd constants; the proof and executable model make no assumptions about an RTL implementation.
This review addresses only the integer identity behind an earlier threshold calculation; it does not prove pipeline latency, RAW handling, or the proposed private 8-cycle pipeline.
The threshold predicate was also checked for 300,000 deterministic random (n,b) pairs and representative edge-count/boundary-counter combinations.
Width bounds: the u32-by-u32 product n*M fits u64; q0*d is at most n; the largest u17*b divisor product is 5,636,053 for d=43.
